title: Three letters, and a call to stop and listen.
subtitle: Alif Lam Mim opens the longest surah
then: Al-Baqarah follows Al-Fatihah and begins the answer to its prayer for guidance. It opens with three separate letters. {idea}Their meaning is known to Allah.{/idea} The Prophet ﷺ called this surah the peak of the Quran.
now: Your phone buzzes, the kettle clicks, someone calls your name. Then three letters you cannot translate. {idea}You are made to stop.{/idea} Not to solve a puzzle, but to notice that what comes next is not ordinary speech.
old: If I cannot understand a word, I can skip past it.
new: Some words are there to quiet me down before something important.
try: Before you read the Quran next, put the phone in another room for those few minutes.

title: The guidance is there; mindfulness is what lets it in.
subtitle: Who actually benefits from the Book
then: The surah answers the prayer of Al-Fatihah: here is the Book, beyond doubt. Ibn Kathir explains that {idea}the Quran is guidance in itself, but its guidance is granted to those with taqwa{/idea}, who avoid what harms and work in obedience.
now: Two people read the same page. One feels nothing and closes the app. The other reads it slowly, worried about a choice at work, and {reward}finds the exact sentence they needed.{/reward} The page did not change. The heart reading it did.
old: If the Quran does not move me, maybe it is not for me.
new: The guidance is complete; my care and fear of Allah is what opens it.
try: Before reading today, say: O Allah, make me one of those this guides. Then read one verse.

title: Trust what you cannot see, then act on it.
subtitle: Unseen faith, prayer, and giving
then: Ibn Mas'ud said the matter of the Prophet ﷺ was clear for those who saw him, and {reward}no one gains better faith than belief in the unseen.{/reward} The Prophet ﷺ spoke of people after the Companions who would believe in him without seeing him.
now: You never saw the Prophet ﷺ. You have never seen an angel or the Hereafter. Yet you set an alarm for Fajr and send money to a cousin who will never pay it back. {idea}That trust, lived out, is exactly what this verse describes.{/idea}
old: My faith is weaker because I never saw anything with my own eyes.
new: Believing without seeing is the very faith this verse honors.
try: Give a small amount today from money you were planning to keep. Tell no one.

title: One chain of messengers, and certainty about what comes next.
subtitle: Believing in all revelation and the Hereafter
then: Ibn 'Abbas explained that these believers {idea}accept what all the messengers brought, without dividing between them.{/idea} Mujahid said four verses at the start of Al-Baqarah describe the believers, and these qualities all depend on one another.
now: You say you believe in the Hereafter. Then the bill comes in, or someone insults you in a group chat, and you act as if this life is the whole story. {reward}Certainty is when the next life changes what you do this afternoon.{/reward}
old: I believe in the Hereafter, in a general way.
new: Real certainty about the Hereafter shows up in today's decisions.
try: Before one reaction today, ask: would I do this if I were certain of tomorrow's reckoning?

title: Success is defined here, and it is not your salary.
subtitle: Guided now, successful in both worlds
then: After describing the believers, the verse gives the result. Ibn Kathir says they follow {idea}a light and insight from Allah{/idea}, and are successful in this world and the Hereafter: {reward}they get what they seek and are saved from what they feared.{/reward}
now: LinkedIn tells you success is a promotion. Instagram says it is a holiday. Your family may say it is a house. This verse quietly gives its own definition. {reward}Guided by your Lord, and safe at the end.{/reward}
old: I will feel successful once I reach my career goals.
new: Being guided by my Lord is already success, whatever my job title says.
try: Write one line tonight: what would success look like if Allah were judging it?

title: Your job is to deliver, not to force the result.
subtitle: When warnings land on closed hearts
then: Ibn 'Abbas said {idea}the Prophet ﷺ was eager for all people to believe.{/idea} Allah told him some would not, whatever he did. Ibn Kathir notes the comfort in this: do not grieve over them, {reward}your duty is only to convey.{/reward}
now: You keep sending your brother articles about quitting smoking. You keep reminding a friend to pray. Nothing changes and you start to feel it is your fault. {idea}Say it kindly, then let go of the outcome.{/idea} Their heart is not in your hands.
old: If they do not change, I did something wrong.
new: My part is to speak well; guiding hearts belongs to Allah.
try: Make dua tonight for one person you keep trying to change, and stop pushing for a day.

title: A heart is sealed one sin at a time.
subtitle: How a heart stops hearing
then: Mujahid held up his open palm and folded one finger for each sin until the hand was closed. {trap}That, he said, is the seal.{/trap} The Prophet ﷺ said a sin leaves a black dot on the heart, and {reward}if the person repents, the heart is polished again.{/reward}
now: The first time you lied on a timesheet, your face went hot. The fifth time, you did not notice. {trap}That quiet is the dot spreading.{/trap} But the hadith is hopeful too. {reward}One sincere turn back, and the heart is polished.{/reward}
old: Small sins do not really change who I am.
new: Every sin dulls the heart a little, and every repentance clears it.
try: Name one small habit you have stopped feeling bad about. Ask Allah's forgiveness for it tonight.

title: Saying I believe is not the same as believing.
subtitle: The first verse on hypocrisy

row.title: the right words
sub: I said it, so I am

then: Hypocrisy appeared in Madinah, not Makkah. After Badr, when Islam grew strong, {trap}some, led by 'Abdullah bin Ubayy, pretended to be Muslim.{/trap} These verses were revealed so the believers would not be fooled by appearances.
now: You post a Ramadan quote while ignoring your mother's calls. You tell your team you value honesty, then fudge the numbers. {trap}The words and the life have drifted apart.{/trap} This verse is a mirror, not a finger to point at others.
old: I say the right things, so I am fine.
new: Allah looks at whether my heart and my words agree.
try: Pick one thing you say you value. Do one small act today that actually matches it.

title: The one you fool in the end is yourself.
subtitle: Deception that only loops back
then: Ibn Kathir explains that the hypocrites showed belief outwardly and hid disbelief, {trap}thinking this would mislead Allah and the believers.{/trap} But no one can deceive Allah. The only person harmed was the one deceiving.
now: You tell your doctor you quit, and you did not. You tell your boss the report is nearly done, and it has not started. {trap}The lie buys a moment, then the cost lands on you.{/trap} With Allah, there is not even the moment.
old: As long as no one finds out, I have not lost anything.
new: Every deception I try ends up costing me, not them.
try: Correct one small untruth you told this week, even a tiny one.

title: Doubt fed with lies grows into a disease.
subtitle: How sickness of the heart increases
then: Ibn 'Abbas and Ibn Mas'ud said the disease here is doubt. {trap}Allah increased it as a fitting result of their lies.{/trap} Ibn Kathir pairs it with the opposite: {reward}those who accept guidance, Allah increases in guidance.{/reward}
now: A small doubt about someone turns into a story you repeat, then into a grudge. The same happens with faith. {trap}What you feed grows.{/trap} {reward}Feed sincerity, and that grows too.{/reward}
old: My doubts just sit there and do not change me.
new: Whatever my heart feeds on, it gets more of.
try: Notice one doubt or bitter thought today and answer it with one true thing you know.

title: Calling damage reform does not make it reform.
subtitle: When people name their harm as peacemaking
then: Abu Al-'Aliyah said corruption on earth is disobeying Allah, and {idea}peace on earth comes through obeying Him.{/idea} Ibn 'Abbas said the hypocrites claimed: {trap}we only want to be friends with both sides.{/trap}
now: You tell one friend what they want to hear about the other, then do the same in reverse, and call it keeping the peace. {trap}You are actually feeding the conflict.{/trap} The verse asks for honest checking of your own motives.
old: I am only trying to keep everyone happy.
new: Peace built on disobedience or two faces is still corruption.
try: Next time you are tempted to tell two people two different stories, tell both the same one.

title: The worst damage is the kind you cannot see yourself doing.
subtitle: Corruption that does not feel like corruption

row.title: I would know if I were wrong

then: This verse answers the claim of the previous one. Ibn Kathir explains that {trap}their behavior, and their claim that it was for peace, was itself the mischief{/trap}, though in their ignorance they could not see it.
now: Your teenager stops talking to you and you are sure it is their phase, not your tone. A colleague quietly leaves and you never wonder why. {trap}Not noticing is not the same as being innocent.{/trap} {idea}Ask someone honest.{/idea}
old: If I were doing harm, I would feel it.
new: Harm can feel normal from the inside, so I need honest eyes on me.
try: Ask one person you trust: is there something I do that hurts others without realizing?

title: Mocking sincere people as simple is its own foolishness.
subtitle: Who the fools really are

row.title: those who do not know it

then: The hypocrites were told to believe as the Companions believed. {trap}They called the Companions fools.{/trap} Ibn Kathir notes that not knowing your own ignorance is {trap}a deeper blindness than one who is aware.{/trap}
now: A colleague prays in the stairwell. Your aunt gives away money she cannot spare. You might roll your eyes and call it naive. {idea}This verse asks you to look again at who is really missing something.{/idea}
old: People with simple, sincere faith are a bit naive.
new: The truly foolish one is the person too proud to see what the sincere see.
try: Think of someone whose faith you once looked down on. Say one sincere good word about them today.

title: One face in the masjid, another face in private.
subtitle: Two audiences, two scripts

row.title: a split self
sub: the private face is the real one

then: The hypocrites declared faith when they met the believers, hoping for a share of any gains. {trap}Alone with their ringleaders, they said: we are with you, we were only mocking.{/trap} Ibn Jarir notes there are devils among humans as well as jinn.
now: At the family dinner you are the pious one. In the office group chat you laugh along at jokes about religious people. {trap}Neither room sees the other.{/trap} The verse asks which version Allah is looking at. {idea}Both.{/idea}
old: Everyone changes a little depending on who they are with.
new: When my private words mock what I praise in public, I have two faces.
try: Notice one conversation today where you would normally laugh along. Stay quiet instead.

title: Being left alone in your wrongdoing is not a win.
subtitle: The mockers are answered
then: Allah answers the mockers in their own terms. Ibn Jarir cites the verse that {trap}a delay in punishment only lets the wrongdoers increase in sin.{/trap} Wandering blindly is the state they are left in.
now: You cut a corner at work and nothing happens. Then another. The silence feels like permission. {trap}It is not.{/trap} {reward}Treat the quiet as a chance to stop, while stopping is easy.{/reward}
old: If nothing bad happened, it must not have been that bad.
new: Being left to carry on in a wrong can be the warning itself.
try: Pick one thing you keep getting away with. Stop it today, before anyone notices.

title: They traded guidance away and made no profit.
subtitle: The worst deal a person can make

row.title: a losing trade
sub: gave the best for the worst

then: Ibn 'Abbas and Ibn Mas'ud said they pursued misguidance and left guidance. Qatadah said: {trap}I have seen them leave guidance for deviation, the community for sects, safety for fear.{/trap} The verse calls it commerce with no profit.
now: You skip Jumu'ah for a meeting that gets cancelled anyway. You drop an old friend who kept you honest for a crowd that is more fun. {trap}It looks like a gain on paper.{/trap} {idea}Count what you actually gave.{/idea}
old: I can afford to let my faith slide for now and get ahead.
new: Swapping guidance for anything is a trade that never pays.
try: Name one thing you traded away for convenience this month. Take one step to get it back.

title: The fire was lit, and then the light was gone.
subtitle: A parable of light that was lost

row.title: a man lights a fire
sub: he can see, he feels safe

then: Ibn Kathir explains the parable: a man lights a fire, it lights up everything around him, he feels safe. {trap}Then it goes out, and only darkness and smoke remain.{/trap} So were those who first believed, then preferred misguidance.
now: Remember the Ramadan when you prayed every night and felt close. The Hajj trip. The month after a loss when the Quran made sense. {trap}Then life got busy and the light quietly went out.{/trap} {reward}Notice it while you still remember what it looked like.{/reward}
old: I was close to Allah once; it will come back by itself.
new: Light I had can be lost if I stop tending it.
try: Bring back one small act from your best spiritual season, just for today.

title: When the heart goes blind, the way back is hard.
subtitle: Deaf, dumb, blind: the end of the fire parable
then: Continuing the parable, they are deaf, dumb and blind. Ibn Kathir links it to the verse that {idea}it is not the eyes that grow blind, but the hearts in the breasts.{/idea} {trap}So they cannot return to the guidance they sold.{/trap}
now: You hear the same reminder at three khutbahs and feel nothing. You want to apologize to your sister but the words will not come out. {trap}That numbness is the warning.{/trap} {reward}While you can still feel it as numbness, you can still turn.{/reward}
old: I just do not feel much these days; it is normal.
new: Losing the ability to hear and respond is a heart problem worth treating now.
try: Say one sentence you have been avoiding to someone today: sorry, or thank you.

title: Fingers in the ears do not stop the storm.
subtitle: A second parable: doubt in a rainstorm
then: This is a parable for those who sometimes know the truth and doubt it at other times. The darkness is doubt, the thunder is fear. Ibn Kathir notes {trap}their caution does not help them, because Allah encompasses all.{/trap}
now: A health scare and you stop opening the clinic's emails. A hard question about your faith and you scroll past every video on it. {trap}Plugging your ears changes nothing outside.{/trap} {idea}Face the question with Allah, not away from Him.{/idea}
old: If I do not look at it, it cannot hurt me.
new: Avoiding the truth does not protect me; turning to Allah does.
try: Open one message or question you have been avoiding, and make dua before you read it.

title: Walking only when it flashes, freezing when it is dark.
subtitle: Faith that only moves in good times
then: Ibn 'Abbas explained: {trap}whenever the hypocrites got a share of Islam's victories, they were content; whenever a calamity came, they were ready to turn back.{/trap} They walked only in the flash.
now: The job offer comes and you pray every prayer on time. The rejection comes and you stop. {trap}Faith that depends on the weather is not yet faith.{/trap} {idea}The dark stretch is where the steps count most.{/idea}
old: I feel close to Allah when things are going well.
new: Real faith keeps walking when the light goes out.
try: If today is a hard day, keep one act of worship exactly as you would on a good day.

title: The One who made you is the One to worship.
subtitle: The first call to all of humanity
then: After describing believers, disbelievers and hypocrites, the surah turns to all people at once. Ibn Kathir explains that {idea}Allah brought them into being after they did not exist{/idea} and surrounded them with blessings, hidden and apparent.
now: You did not choose your birthday, your heartbeat, or the parents who raised you. You woke up this morning without arranging it. {idea}The reason to worship is not a family custom. It is that someone made you.{/idea}
old: I pray because it is what my family does.
new: I worship Allah because He created me and everyone before me.
try: Put your hand on your chest for ten seconds. Feel the heartbeat you did not start. Say alhamdulillah.

title: Bed, roof, rain, food: and you still set up rivals?
subtitle: The provider alone deserves worship
then: Allah is Creator, Sustainer and Provider, so He alone deserves worship. The Prophet ﷺ called it the worst sin {trap}to set up an equal with Allah while He created you.{/trap} He even taught to say: {idea}what Allah wills, then what so-and-so wills.{/idea}
now: Payday comes and you think: my boss pays me. The test results come back clear and you thank only the doctor. {trap}Small rivals creep into how we talk.{/trap} {idea}The salary and the doctor are real, but they come after Him.{/idea}
old: My income comes from my employer.
new: Every provision, through whoever brings it, comes from Allah first.
try: Next time you thank someone today, quietly thank Allah first.

title: If you doubt it, bring one surah like it.
subtitle: The challenge the Quran sets
then: After proving Allah's oneness, the surah proves the prophethood. {idea}If it is not from Allah, produce something like it, with any help you want.{/idea} Mujahid said the witnesses meant wise and eloquent people. The challenge repeats across the Quran.
now: Someone at university tells you the Quran is just old poetry. You feel defensive. {idea}The Quran is calm about it: here is the test, try it.{/idea} Your faith does not need to panic at a question.
old: When someone doubts the Quran, I feel I must win the argument.
new: The Quran sets its own test and stands on it; I can answer calmly.
try: Read one short surah aloud slowly today and notice one thing about how it is put together.

title: You will not meet the challenge, so take the warning.
subtitle: What follows when the challenge fails

row.title: a reason to accept
sub: the proof is in front of you

then: The challenge of the previous verse comes with a prediction: {idea}you will never be able to do it.{/idea} {trap}So the warning is to fear the Fire prepared for those who reject.{/trap}
now: You know the Quran is true. You have felt it. Yet days pass and you live as if it were just a book on the shelf. {trap}Knowing and ignoring is the risk here.{/trap} {reward}The warning is mercy, said early, while there is time.{/reward}
old: Warnings about the Fire are for people who do not believe at all.
new: The warning is for anyone who knows the truth and still sets it aside.
try: Choose one verse you know but do not act on. Act on it once today.

title: It looks familiar, then tastes better than anything before.
subtitle: Good news for those who believe and do good
then: After the warning comes good news, the Quran pairing the two as it often does. Abu Al-'Aliyah said the fruits of Paradise {reward}look like each other but the taste is different.{/reward} 'Ikrimah said they resemble this world's fruit but taste better.
now: The first bite of a mango in summer. The meal your grandmother made. You chase that taste again and it is never quite the same. {reward}This verse describes a place where every bite is the first one, and it never ends.{/reward}
old: Paradise is a reward far away that I cannot really picture.
new: Every good taste here is a small hint of something far better waiting.
try: Eat one thing slowly today, savor it, and say: O Allah, give me the better one.

title: Even a mosquito can carry a lesson, if you are listening.
subtitle: The same parable guides some and misleads others
then: When Allah gave the parables of the fire and the rainstorm, the hypocrites said Allah is too exalted for such examples. {idea}This verse answered them.{/idea} Mujahid said the believers accept parables large or small, {reward}and Allah guides them by these parables.{/reward}
now: A sentence in a children's book. A bee on your windowsill. A stranger's kindness at a bus stop. {trap}You can call it too small to matter{/trap}, or {idea}let it teach you something about Allah.{/idea} The difference is in you.
old: Small, ordinary things have nothing deep to teach me.
new: Allah can teach me through the smallest thing, if my heart is open.
try: Notice one tiny creature or small moment today and ask what it shows you about its Maker.

title: Broken promises, broken family ties, and a broken world.
subtitle: Three marks of those who lose
then: Ibn Kathir explains the covenant as Allah's covenant with His creation: {idea}to obey Him and avoid what He forbade{/idea}. He links the verse to Surah Ar-Ra'd, where those who join what Allah ordered joined are {reward}good to their relatives and do not cut kinship.{/reward}
now: Your uncle said something hurtful at a wedding three years ago and you have not spoken since. {trap}Blocking his number felt like the end of the problem.{/trap} This verse puts cutting family ties next to breaking faith with Allah.
old: Cutting off a difficult relative is just protecting my peace.
new: Keeping ties Allah told me to keep is part of keeping my promise to Him.
try: Send a short, kind message to one relative you have drifted from. Nothing more is needed.

title: You were nothing, then alive, then gone, then alive again.
subtitle: The four stages no one escapes
then: Ibn 'Abbas said: {idea}you did not exist before; you were nothing until Allah created you.{/idea} Then He brings death and brings you back at the Resurrection. The verse asks how anyone could deny the One who controls every stage.
now: You look at a baby photo of yourself. A hundred years before it, there was no you at all. A hundred years from now, your phone contacts will not know your name. {idea}The One who did the first step can do the last.{/idea}
old: My life began at birth and ends at death.
new: My story starts before I existed and continues after I die, all in His hands.
try: Look at an old photo of yourself today and remember: He brought me from nothing.

title: Everything on earth was made with you in mind.
subtitle: The earth for you, the heavens above, all known
then: After the proof within ourselves, the surah gives a proof we can see: the earth and the heavens. Ibn Kathir links it to the verse: {idea}should not He who created know?{/idea} {reward}His knowledge covers all He made.{/reward}
now: The water from your tap, the rice on your plate, the air in a crowded train. You use a thousand created things before lunch. {reward}None of them were accidents, and none of your worries are hidden from the One who made them.{/reward}
old: The universe is huge; my small life does not register.
new: The One who made everything for me also knows everything about me.
try: Drink one glass of water slowly today and say alhamdulillah for it.

title: The angels asked why; Allah said, I know what you do not.
subtitle: Humans placed on earth, generation after generation
then: Ibn Kathir says khalifah here means people succeeding one another on earth. {idea}The angels' question was not envy or dispute, but a request to learn the wisdom.{/idea} Allah answered that He knows what they do not.
now: Your life took a turn you did not want: the move, the diagnosis, the job you lost. You ask why. {idea}Asking to understand is allowed; even the angels asked.{/idea} {reward}And the answer starts with trusting that He knows more.{/reward}
old: If I question what happened to me, I am being ungrateful.
new: I can ask Allah why, humbly, and trust He knows what I cannot see.
try: Bring one why to Allah in dua tonight, honestly, then end with: You know best.

title: Allah taught Adam the names of everything.
subtitle: Knowledge as the first honor given to humans
then: Ibn 'Abbas said Adam was taught the names people use: {idea}human, animal, sky, earth, sea, horse{/idea}, even the plate and the pot. Ibn Kathir says this showed {reward}Adam's virtue over the angels in knowledge.{/reward}
now: Your child learns a new word and runs to show you. You learn a skill at work and suddenly see how things connect. {reward}The ability to name, learn and understand is a gift from Allah, given first to Adam.{/reward}
old: Learning is just a way to get a job.
new: The ability to learn is an honor Allah gave humans from the start.
try: Learn the meaning of one word in a verse or dua you say every day.

title: We know only what You taught us.
subtitle: The angels' humble answer

row.title: say: I do not know
sub: and praise the One who does

then: Asked for the names, the angels did not guess. {idea}They glorified Allah and said they know only what He has taught them.{/idea} They returned all knowledge to the Knowing, the Wise.
now: Your manager asks a question in a meeting and you do not know. Your child asks about death. {trap}The urge is to sound sure.{/trap} {idea}The angels show a better way: admit it, and turn to the One who knows.{/idea}
old: Admitting I do not know makes me look weak.
new: Saying I only know what Allah taught me is the honest and humble answer.
try: The next time you do not know something today, say so plainly instead of guessing.

title: He knows what you show and what you hide.
subtitle: Adam names them, and the wisdom is shown
then: Adam told the angels the names. Ibn Kathir says this showed the angels {idea}the wisdom of creating the khalifah{/idea} that they had asked about. Allah reminded them that He knows the unseen, and what they reveal and conceal.
now: There is the you in your profile picture, and the you at 2 a.m. with your worries. {idea}Allah knows both.{/idea} {reward}That can feel frightening, or it can feel like relief: someone finally sees the whole picture.{/reward}
old: No one really knows what is going on inside me.
new: Allah knows what I show and what I hide, and that is a comfort.
try: Tell Allah one thing tonight that you have not told anyone.

title: All bowed except one, and pride was the reason.
subtitle: The first refusal
then: Ibn 'Abbas said Iblis was {trap}among the most active worshippers and knowledgeable, and this made him arrogant.{/trap} Qatadah said: {idea}the obedience was for Allah, and the prostration was before Adam.{/idea}
now: You have prayed for years. You know more than the new brother at the masjid. Then someone corrects you and you bristle. {trap}That is the oldest trap there is.{/trap} {idea}Worship that makes you proud has turned against you.{/idea}
old: My years of practice put me above being told what to do.
new: Worship should make me humbler; pride can undo all of it.
try: Accept one correction today, from anyone, without defending yourself.

title: Everything was allowed, except one tree.
subtitle: Paradise, plenty, and a single limit
then: Allah honored Adam and let him live in Paradise with his wife, eating whatever they wished. {trap}The one tree was a test.{/trap} Ibn Jarir said the correct view is simply that it was a certain tree; {idea}its type is not what matters.{/idea}
now: Your fridge is full and you want the one thing your doctor said to avoid. Your feed has a thousand good things and you click the one that harms you. {reward}Look at how much is open to you.{/reward} The limit is small; the plenty is huge.
old: The rules of my faith feel like a long list of no.
new: Almost everything is open to me; the limits are few and for my good.
try: List five permitted good things you enjoyed today. Thank Allah for each.

title: Satan made them slip, and life on earth began.
subtitle: The fall, and a home for a while
then: Satan caused Adam and his wife to slip from the Garden. Allah sent them down with enmity between them and Satan. {idea}The earth was given as a dwelling and enjoyment for a time.{/idea}
now: You are decorating a new flat, paying off a car, planning the next ten years. All good. {idea}But this verse whispers: for a time.{/idea} {trap}And the one who made your parents slip is still whispering too.{/trap}
old: This world is where I am meant to settle permanently.
new: Earth is a temporary stay, and I have an enemy who wants me to forget that.
try: Before you buy something today, ask: will this matter in the next life?

title: Adam slipped, then Allah gave him the words to come back.
subtitle: The first repentance

row.title: I must earn my way back

then: Many early scholars said the words were: {idea}Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves; if You do not forgive us and have mercy on us, we will be among the losers.{/idea} Ibn 'Abbas reported Adam asking: {reward}does not Your mercy precede Your anger? He was told, yes.{/reward}
now: You snapped at your kids, or broke a promise to Allah for the hundredth time. {trap}Shame says do not even try.{/trap} {reward}But Allah handed Adam the very words to come back with.{/reward} You can use them tonight.
old: After what I did, I do not even know how to start asking forgiveness.
new: Allah gives me the words to return, and He is the One who accepts.
try: Say Adam's dua tonight: Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves, forgive us and have mercy on us.

title: Guidance will come; follow it, and fear and grief lose their grip.
subtitle: The promise given at the start of human life
then: As Adam, his wife and Satan were sent down, Allah promised to send books and messengers. Abu Al-'Aliyah said guidance means {idea}the prophets, messengers, clear signs and plain explanation.{/idea} {reward}No fear about the Hereafter, no grief over this world.{/reward}
now: You lie awake replaying a conversation and worrying about next month. {trap}Fear about what is coming, grief over what is gone.{/trap} This verse makes a promise to people who follow His guidance: {reward}both lose their grip.{/reward}
old: Feeling safe depends on how my plans turn out.
new: Following Allah's guidance is what frees me from fear and grief.
try: When a worry comes today, answer it with one line of guidance you already know.

title: Turning away from the signs is a choice with an end.
subtitle: The other side of the promise to Adam's children
then: Right after the promise to whoever follows guidance comes its opposite. Ibn Kathir pairs it with the verse that {trap}whoever turns from My reminder will have a hard life{/trap}. Those who deny the signs remain in the Fire with no way out.
now: You know the reminder is true. You hear it in a khutbah, read it in a verse your friend shares. {trap}Then you scroll past.{/trap} The verse is sober about where a lifetime of scrolling past leads. {reward}The door to follow is still open today.{/reward}
old: Ignoring reminders is harmless as long as I do not reject them outright.
new: Turning away again and again is a path, and it has a destination.
try: The next reminder that reaches you today, stop and act on one word of it.

title: Remember the favor, keep your side, fear only Him.
subtitle: A call to the children of a righteous father
then: Israel is Prophet Ya'qub. Ibn Kathir says the call is like saying: {idea}O children of a righteous servant, be like your father and follow the truth.{/idea} Abu Al-'Aliyah said the favor was sending them prophets and books.
now: Your grandfather was the imam of the village. Your mother never missed a prayer. {trap}It is easy to feel their goodness counts for you.{/trap} {idea}This verse says: honor them by becoming like them.{/idea}
old: I come from a religious family, so I am basically fine.
new: A righteous family is a reminder to live up to, not a cover for me.
try: Pick one good habit of a parent or grandparent and do it today in their honor.

title: Do not sell guidance for a small price.
subtitle: Believing what confirms what you already have

row.title: do not be first to deny
a small price
sub: anything is small next to it

then: Those who had earlier scripture were told to believe in the Quran, {idea}which confirms what was already with them.{/idea} They were warned {trap}not to be the first to reject it, nor to trade Allah's signs for a small gain.{/trap}
now: You stay quiet about the truth in a meeting to keep your bonus. You skip a prayer to finish a sale. {trap}It always feels like a good deal at the time.{/trap} {idea}Whatever the price, it is small compared to what you sold.{/idea}
old: Bending a little on my principles for a big gain is just being practical.
new: Anything I get by selling out on Allah's guidance is a small price.
try: Notice one moment today when you are tempted to trade a principle for comfort. Keep the principle.

title: Half truth mixed with a lie is still a lie.
subtitle: Mixing truth with falsehood, and hiding what you know
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah forbade two things here and {idea}ordered them to make the truth known and explain it.{/idea} Ibn 'Abbas said: {trap}do not mix the truth with falsehood, and the facts with lies.{/trap}
now: Your CV says you led the project. You were on the team. The review you write online is true, minus the part that matters. {trap}A fact with a lie folded in.{/trap} {idea}Or silence when you know someone is being misled.{/idea}
old: As long as nothing I said was an outright lie, I was honest.
new: Mixing truth with spin, or hiding what I know, is not honesty.
try: Correct one exaggeration you have made, in a bio, a story, or a message.

title: Pray, give, and bow together with others.
subtitle: Worship joined to a community
then: Muqatil said the command meant {idea}to pray behind the Prophet ﷺ, give zakah, and bow down with his community.{/idea} Ibn Kathir explains it as a call to be with, and among, the believers.
now: You pray at home, alone, between emails. That is good. {idea}But there is something in standing shoulder to shoulder in a row of strangers.{/idea} The verse does not only say bow. It says bow with those who bow.
old: My worship is between me and Allah; other people do not matter.
new: Worship is personal, and it is also shared with the people who bow beside me.
try: Pray one prayer today with others, at a masjid, at work, or with your family.

title: You tell others to do good and forget yourself.
subtitle: Preaching without practicing
then: Ibn Jurayj said this was about people who {trap}told others to pray and fast but did not do it themselves.{/trap} His advice: {idea}whoever commands righteousness, let him be among the first to do it.{/idea}
now: You forward the hadith about patience, then shout at the driver who cut you off. You lecture your kids about screen time from behind your phone. {trap}The words go out, but do not come home.{/trap}
old: Reminding others is good, even if I am not doing it myself.
new: The first person my reminders should reach is me.
try: Think of the last piece of advice you gave someone. Do it yourself today.

title: When it is heavy, lean on patience and prayer.
subtitle: Two kinds of help, and why prayer feels hard
then: 'Umar bin Al-Khattab said there are two kinds of patience: {reward}good patience when disaster strikes, and better patience in avoiding what Allah forbade.{/reward} Prayer is among the best means of help. {trap}It is heavy, except for the humble.{/trap}
now: Bad news on the phone. A craving you have fought for weeks. Your first move is to scroll, eat, vent. {idea}This verse offers two other tools: hold on, and go pray.{/idea} If prayer feels heavy, that is exactly what the verse said.
old: Prayer is the last thing I feel like doing when I am stressed.
new: Prayer and patience are the help, especially when I do not feel like it.
try: When the next stressful moment hits today, pray two rak'ahs before doing anything else.

title: Prayer gets lighter when you know who you are meeting.
subtitle: What makes the humble different
then: The previous verse said prayer is heavy except for the humble. {idea}This verse explains them: they are certain they will meet their Lord and return to Him.{/idea} That certainty is what makes the weight bearable.
now: You drag yourself to Fajr like a chore. Now picture going to meet someone you love, who is waiting for you. {idea}The alarm is the same. What changes is knowing who you are going to.{/idea}
old: I need more discipline to pray properly.
new: Remembering that I will meet Allah makes prayer lighter.
try: Before your next prayer, take ten seconds to remember: I am about to stand before my Lord.

title: Being chosen is a reminder, not a privilege to coast on.
subtitle: Favor given to earlier generations
then: Allah reminds the Children of Israel of the favor given to their forefathers. Abu Al-'Aliyah said it was {reward}kingship, messengers and books given to them over the kingdoms of their time{/reward}, for every period has its nation.
now: You were born into faith, or found it. You have a Quran on your phone in your own language. {reward}That is a favor many never had.{/reward} {idea}The verse asks you to remember it, not to feel superior because of it.{/idea}
old: Being Muslim makes me better than others.
new: Being given guidance is a favor that asks for gratitude and effort, not pride.
try: Thank Allah today for one specific way He guided you that you did not earn.

title: On that Day, no one can carry you.
subtitle: No substitute, no ransom, no rescue
then: After the favors, a warning. Ibn Kathir cites the verse that {trap}no father can avail his son, nor a son his father{/trap}, and calls it a great warning. No one bears another's burden.
now: You assume your mother's duas will cover you. Your father's charity. Your spouse's piety. {trap}They are blessings, but they are theirs.{/trap} {idea}On that Day, you stand with what you did.{/idea} {reward}So start building it today.{/reward}
old: My family's goodness will help me on the Day.
new: On that Day I stand with my own deeds, so I must build them now.
try: Do one good deed today that is only yours: a private charity, a quiet prayer.

title: Saved from the worst, and the saving was a test too.
subtitle: Rescue from Pharaoh's cruelty
then: Ibn Kathir says Pharaoh, fearing a man from the Children of Israel would end his rule, {trap}ordered every newborn boy killed and forced them into humiliating labor.{/trap} {reward}Allah saved them through Musa.{/reward} The verse calls it all a great trial.
now: You came through the illness, the redundancy, the hard years. {reward}You are on the other side now.{/reward} {idea}The test is not only how you held up in the hard part. It is also what you do with the rescue.{/idea}
old: Once the hard time is over, the test is over.
new: Being saved from hardship is also a test of how grateful I will be.
try: Remember one hardship Allah brought you through. Do one thing today out of gratitude for it.

title: The sea split, and they watched the danger disappear.
subtitle: A rescue seen with their own eyes
then: This is part of the favor Allah told them to remember. {reward}He separated the sea, saved them, and drowned Pharaoh's people{/reward} {idea}while they were looking on.{/idea} They did not hear about it. They saw it.
now: The job came through on the last day. The scan came back clear. The money arrived the week rent was due. {trap}A month later, you call it luck.{/trap} {idea}You were looking on. Remember who parted the sea.{/idea}
old: That close call worked out because I was lucky.
new: The rescues I have seen with my own eyes were from Allah.
try: Write down one rescue in your life you witnessed. Keep it where you will see it.

title: Forty nights away, and they made a calf.
subtitle: How fast people slip once the guide is gone
then: Musa went to meet his Lord for forty nights, soon after they crossed the sea. {trap}In his absence, they took the calf for worship, and so wronged themselves.{/trap} The miracle at the sea was still fresh.
now: Ramadan ends and by Shawwal the night prayers are gone. Your teacher moves away and your study habit stops. {trap}When the person who held you steady leaves, it is shocking how fast things slip.{/trap}
old: After a strong spiritual moment, I will stay on track.
new: Even after great signs, I can slip fast once my support is gone.
try: Set one small habit today that does not depend on anyone else to keep it going.

title: Even after the calf, Allah forgave them.
subtitle: Forgiveness meant to produce gratitude
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah reminds them: {reward}remember My favor when I forgave you for worshipping the calf.{/reward} {idea}The purpose of the forgiveness is named in the verse itself: that you might be grateful.{/idea}
now: Someone forgave you for something big: a spouse, a parent, a friend you let down. {reward}You felt the relief.{/reward} {idea}The way to honor that forgiveness is to live differently because of it.{/idea} Allah's forgiveness asks the same.
old: Once I am forgiven, the matter is closed.
new: Being forgiven is a gift meant to make me grateful and change me.
try: Think of one sin you believe Allah forgave you. Thank Him for it in your own words.

title: A Book and a criterion to tell right from wrong.
subtitle: What Musa was given after the sea
then: After the sea, Musa was given the Tawrah and the furqan. Ibn Kathir says the furqan is {idea}that which separates truth from falsehood, guidance from deviation.{/idea} It was given so that they might be guided.
now: A deal that looks fine but feels off. A friend's request that is half right. {trap}Your feelings change by the hour.{/trap} {idea}Revelation gives you a fixed line to measure against when your own sense is foggy.{/idea}
old: I will know what is right by how it feels.
new: Allah gave a criterion so I do not have to guess what is right.
try: Facing a choice today, look up what the Quran or Sunnah says before deciding.

title: Return to the One who made you, and He accepts.
subtitle: A grave sin and a grave repentance
then: Musa told his people they had wronged themselves by the calf. Ibn Kathir says naming Allah as Bari', the Creator, {trap}alerts them to the enormity of their error{/trap}: turning to others after He made them. The repentance asked was severe. {reward}Then He accepted it.{/reward}
now: Some sins you laugh off. Others you know, deep down, were a turning away from the One who made you. {idea}Those deserve a real repentance, not a quick sorry.{/idea} {reward}And the verse ends on the same note: He accepts, He is Merciful.{/reward}
old: A quick astaghfirullah covers anything I do.
new: Serious wrongs call for serious repentance, and Allah truly accepts it.
try: Think of one serious wrong you have only half repented from. Sit with it tonight and repent fully.

title: We will not believe until we see Allah ourselves.
subtitle: Demanding proof on your own terms

row.title: trust what He showed
sub: some things no one can bear

then: Ibn Jurayj said they asked to see Allah directly, {trap}which neither they nor anyone else can bear.{/trap} As-Suddi said they were seized and died, and Musa stood crying and praying for them. This came after the sea, the clouds and the Book.
now: You have seen your prayers answered, a child born healthy, a door open at the last moment. {trap}Yet part of you says: I will fully trust when I get one more sign.{/trap} {idea}The signs are already there. Asking for more on your terms is the problem.{/idea}
old: If Allah showed me one clear sign, I would never doubt again.
new: I have been shown enough; demanding proof on my terms is not faith.
try: List three signs of Allah's care you have already seen. Read the list when doubt comes.

title: Brought back to life to try again, with gratitude.
subtitle: A second chance after death
then: As-Suddi said Allah brought them back to life one man at a time while the rest watched. Ar-Rabi' bin Anas said {reward}they were raised so they could finish out their lives.{/reward} {idea}The verse names the purpose: gratitude.{/idea}
now: The car crash you walked away from. The surgery that could have gone the other way. The night you were sure was your last. {reward}You got more time.{/reward} {idea}This verse asks what the extra days are for.{/idea}
old: I survived that, so life just goes on as before.
new: Every second chance is extra time to live gratefully.
try: Recall a time you nearly lost your life or health. Spend ten minutes today thanking Allah for it.

title: Shade, food from the sky, and still they wronged themselves.
subtitle: Daily provision in the wilderness
then: During the years of wandering, white clouds shaded them from the sun. Qatadah said {reward}the manna fell like snow, whiter than milk and sweeter than honey{/reward}, and each took enough for the day. {trap}Still, they did not wrong Allah; they wronged themselves.{/trap}
now: Your food arrives every day: from a shop, a salary, a parent. You rarely think about how. {reward}It is provision, as real as manna.{/reward} {trap}Forgetting to be grateful does not hurt Allah. It just makes you poorer inside.{/trap}
old: My daily needs are just met; there is nothing special about it.
new: My daily food is provision from Allah, and ingratitude only harms me.
try: Before your next meal, name where it came from and say alhamdulillah with meaning.

title: Walk into success bowing, and ask for forgiveness.
subtitle: How to enter a victory
then: After forty years of wandering, they were given the holy land. Ibn Kathir says they were told to enter {idea}bowing in gratitude for victory, admitting their sins and asking forgiveness.{/idea} He links it to Surah An-Nasr: at victory, glorify and seek forgiveness.
now: You get the promotion, the degree, the keys to the house. {trap}The natural move is to post it and feel proud.{/trap} {idea}This verse teaches another way to walk through that door: humble, thankful, asking Allah to forgive what you got wrong on the way.{/idea}
old: When I succeed, I have earned the right to celebrate myself.
new: Success is a moment to bow, thank Allah, and ask forgiveness.
try: For your next win, however small, pray two rak'ahs of thanks and say astaghfirullah.

title: They changed one word and mocked the whole command.
subtitle: Twisting an instruction into a joke
then: The Prophet ﷺ said they were told to enter bowing and say hittah, {trap}but they entered dragging themselves on their behinds and changed the word to habbah, a seed in a hair.{/trap} Ibn Kathir says they twisted the command in tongue and deed.
now: You turn a verse into a meme. You repeat a dua in a mocking voice. You do the prayer, but in a way that makes clear you think it is silly. {trap}It looks small.{/trap} {idea}Treat what Allah commands with respect, even in jokes.{/idea}
old: A little humor about religious instructions is harmless.
new: Twisting Allah's words into a joke is a form of defiance.
try: If you see a joke today that mocks a verse or dua, do not share it.

title: Twelve springs from one stone, and a warning not to spoil it.
subtitle: An answered prayer for water
then: Allah answered Musa's prayer for water: {reward}twelve springs gushed from a stone, one for each tribe{/reward}, with food and drink without effort. Ibn Kathir explains the warning: {trap}do not return the favor with disobedience that makes favors disappear.{/trap}
now: Your health, your marriage, the job you prayed for. {reward}Each was an answered prayer once.{/reward} {trap}Then the late nights, the neglect, the small sins start draining them.{/trap} The verse says: enjoy it, and do not spoil it.
old: Once Allah gives me something, it is mine to keep however I live.
new: Blessings stay through gratitude and can drain away through sin.
try: Name one answered prayer in your life. Do one thing today to protect it.

title: Bored of the better, they asked for the lesser.
subtitle: Trading the best for the ordinary
then: Al-Hasan Al-Basri said {trap}they were bored with their food and remembered their old diet of lentils, onions and garlic.{/trap} Musa asked: {idea}would you exchange the better for the lower?{/idea} The verse traces how repeated disobedience led to humiliation and anger.
now: You have a kind spouse, a quiet home, a steady faith. {trap}It starts to feel dull, and you miss the old nights out, the old crowd.{/trap} {idea}Boredom with a blessing is often the first step to trading it away.{/idea}
old: I am just bored; wanting something different is natural.
new: Boredom with what Allah gave me can lead me to trade the better for the lower.
try: Pick one blessing that has started to feel boring. Find one new thing to appreciate in it today.

title: Faith in Allah, the Last Day, and good deeds: the constant.
subtitle: What saved the righteous in every era
then: After describing those who defied, the verse turns to the righteous of earlier nations. Ibn Kathir explains that {idea}before the Prophet ﷺ was sent, whoever followed the guidance of his own prophet was on the right path{/idea}, and after him, salvation is in following him ﷺ.
now: You carry the name Muslim on your passport and in your family. {trap}The name alone does not do the work.{/trap} {idea}This verse names what has always mattered: real faith in Allah and the Last Day, shown in good deeds.{/idea}
old: Belonging to the right group is what saves me.
new: What Allah rewards is true faith and righteous deeds, not a label.
try: Do one good deed today purely because you believe in the Last Day.

title: Hold what you were given with both hands.
subtitle: A promise made under the mountain
then: Allah reminds the Children of Israel of the pledge He took from them to worship Him alone and follow His Messengers. The mountain was raised over their heads so they would take that pledge seriously. {idea}Hold firmly to what We gave you, and remember what is in it.{/idea} The scholars explained this as reading the Torah and acting on it.
now: You downloaded the Quran app months ago. You opened it during a hard week, felt something, then let it slide. {trap}Guidance held with two fingers slips out easily.{/trap} {idea}Holding it with strength looks like a small, steady habit, not a burst.{/idea}
old: I believe in it, so that is enough.
new: Guidance has to be gripped and remembered, or it slips away.
try: Pick one verse you already know and act on it once today on purpose.

title: They turned away, and mercy still caught them.
subtitle: What stood between them and loss

row.title: Allah's favor
sub: the only thing between them and loss

then: Even after that solemn pledge, they deviated and broke it. Ibn Kathir explains that Allah's grace showed itself by forgiving them and sending them Prophets again. {reward}Without that mercy they would have been among the losers{/reward}, in this life and the next.
now: You promised yourself after Ramadan that things would be different. By the second week you were back to the old scroll at midnight. {trap}You broke it.{/trap} {reward}And the door is still open tonight.{/reward} That is not your achievement. It is His favor.
old: I have broken my promise to Allah too many times to come back.
new: The fact that I can still turn back is itself His mercy at work.
try: Tonight, before sleep, quietly renew one promise you broke. No speech, just a sentence.

title: A clever trick around a clear limit.
subtitle: The Sabbath-breakers and their nets

row.title: technically allowed
sub: we did not fish on Saturday

then: A village by the sea was told to keep the Sabbath. The fish came in plenty on Saturdays, so they set nets and pools before the day and collected the catch after it. {trap}Their deceit looked lawful on the surface.{/trap} Allah turned them into apes, despised. Ibn Kathir notes the Prophet ﷺ warned against making forbidden things lawful by the lowest tricks.
now: The rule at work says no side deals with clients. So you use your cousin's name. The diet says no sweets, so you call it a protein bar. {trap}You found the loophole.{/trap} {idea}But you know what the line was for.{/idea}
old: If it is technically within the rules, I am fine.
new: A trick that keeps the letter and breaks the point is still crossing the line.
try: Name one loophole you use. Ask yourself honestly what the rule was protecting.

title: Their story was kept so yours could change.
subtitle: A warning for then and for later

row.title: a reminder
sub: so it does not happen to me

then: Allah made that village an example for the towns around it and for those who came later, by preserving the story. Ibn Kathir says {idea}those who have taqwa should be aware of that behavior, so the same does not befall them.{/idea} The point is not the past. It is the listener.
now: You read about a colleague fired for fudging expense claims. Your first thought is how foolish they were. {trap}Your second thought should be the receipts in your own drawer.{/trap} {idea}Stories about others are mirrors.{/idea}
old: Stories of punished people are about bad people, not me.
new: The story was kept for me, so I can check myself before it is too late.
try: Next time you hear of someone's downfall, ask one quiet question: where am I doing a small version of that?

title: A simple command met with Are you mocking us?
subtitle: The start of the story of the cow

row.title: you mock us
sub: it makes no sense to us

then: A man was killed and his body left at another's door. The people nearly fought each other, until the wise among them said to go to Musa. He told them {idea}Allah commands you to slaughter a cow.{/idea} They answered, {trap}Do you take us in ridicule?{/trap} Musa sought refuge in Allah from being among the ignorant.
now: Your doctor tells you to walk twenty minutes a day for your blood pressure. It sounds too small for something so serious. {trap}You almost laugh.{/trap} {idea}Sometimes the answer is simple and the problem is our pride.{/idea}
old: If an instruction does not make sense to me, it must be a joke.
new: Not seeing the reason for a command is not the same as there being none.
try: Do one small good thing today that you have been dismissing as too simple to matter.

title: Every question they asked made it harder.
subtitle: The first round of unneeded questions
then: Ibn Abbas and Ubaydah said that had they slaughtered any cow, it would have been enough. {trap}They made it difficult, so Allah made it more difficult.{/trap} The first answer: neither old nor young, but at its strongest age. And Musa added, {idea}so do what you are commanded.{/idea}
now: You know you should call your mother and apologize. But first you need to know exactly what to say, what time she is free, whether she is still upset. {trap}A week passes in preparation.{/trap} {idea}Just do what you were told.{/idea}
old: I am not delaying, I just need more details first.
new: Some questions are a way of not doing the thing.
try: Take one task you keep researching instead of doing and do the first step now.

title: Now the color. The search gets narrower.
subtitle: The second round of questions
then: Having been told the age, they came back for the color. The answer: {idea}a yellow cow, bright in color, pleasing to those who see it.{/idea} Ibn Kathir frames this whole exchange as their stubbornness and the many unnecessary questions they asked. {trap}The more they asked, the rarer the cow became.{/trap}
now: Your friend asks for help moving. You say yes, but which day, and how many boxes, and is there a lift. Each question is reasonable. {trap}Together they are a slow no.{/trap} {idea}Sometimes the kind thing is to just show up.{/idea}
old: Asking more questions only makes me more precise.
new: When I keep asking after the answer is clear, I am making my own path harder.
try: Next time you are asked to help today, say yes without the extra questions once.

title: All cows look alike to us, they said again.
subtitle: The third round, and an if Allah wills
then: A third time they asked what the cow was, saying {trap}all cows look alike to us.{/trap} Ibn Kathir explains they meant cows were plentiful, so describe it further. They added, {reward}if Allah wills, we will be guided.{/reward} Even after all the answers, Ibn Abbas said, they did not want to slaughter it.
now: You tell yourself all the charities look the same, so you will give once you find the right one. All the masjid classes look alike, so you will join when the perfect one opens. {trap}The sameness is a reason to wait.{/trap} {idea}Pick one. The guidance is in the doing.{/idea}
old: I cannot choose because everything looks the same.
new: When everything looks the same, any honest choice is better than no choice.
try: Choose one good option you have been comparing endlessly and commit to it today.

title: Any cow would have done. They asked until it was rare.
subtitle: How extra questions made a simple command heavy

row.title: we just want clarity
sub: to be sure we get it right

row.title: delay
sub: they nearly did not do it

then: Musa told his people to slaughter a cow. Ibn Abbas said {idea}any cow would have been enough.{/idea} They kept asking about its age, its colour, its work. Each answer narrowed it. In the end they did it, but {trap}they almost did not.{/trap}
now: You know the thing you should do. Call your mother. Start the prayer. Apologise. Instead you ask: what is the exact rule, what if, which way is best. You read three more articles on your phone. {trap}The questions become the reason it never happens.{/trap}
old: I just need a few more details before I start.
new: Sometimes my questions are a way of not doing what I already know.
try: Pick one clear good thing you have been researching instead of doing. Do the simplest version today.

title: They hid a killing. Allah was going to bring it out.
subtitle: The real reason behind the cow

row.title: if no one knows, it is buried

then: A man was killed among the Children of Israel and no one would own it. {trap}Some said: you killed him. Others said: no, you did.{/trap} The verse names the real point of the whole cow story: {idea}Allah was going to bring out what they were hiding.{/idea}
now: Something went missing at work and you know who took it. Or you are the one who broke the thing and let the blame float around the family. Everyone points sideways. {idea}Hidden things have a way of coming out.{/idea} Better that you bring it out first.
old: If nobody can prove it, it stays buried.
new: What I hide is already known, and Allah can bring it into the open.
try: If you have let someone else carry blame for something small you did, tell them today.

title: A piece of the cow touched the dead man. He spoke.
subtitle: A small sign of the great rising
then: They struck the dead man with part of the cow and he came back to life. Ibn Kathir notes we are not told which part, because it does not help us. The point is bigger: {idea}this is how Allah brings the dead to life.{/idea} He lists five such scenes in this surah, all pointing to {reward}the Resurrection.{/reward}
now: You stand by a grave after a funeral. Dust, silence, the car park. It feels final. Then spring comes and the bare tree outside your window is green again. {idea}Bringing back is not hard for the One who made it the first time.{/idea}
old: Death looks like the end of the story.
new: Every sign of life returning is a small rehearsal of the Day the dead rise.
try: Next time you see a plant regrow or rain on dry ground, stop and think of the Resurrection for a moment.

title: Some stones soften. Their hearts did not.
subtitle: A heart can get harder than rock
then: They had just seen a dead man stand up and speak. Ibn Abbas said his relatives still denied killing him. {trap}After that, their hearts hardened.{/trap} The verse compares them to stone, then reminds that {idea}even stones split, let water out, and fall in awe of Allah.{/idea}
now: You heard a talk that made you cry. A week later you are back to the same scrolling, the same sharp words to your spouse. Then another reminder, and you feel it less. {trap}Hardness grows slowly.{/trap} The Quran later warns believers: has the time not come for hearts to soften?
old: I have heard all this before, it does not move me anymore.
new: If nothing moves me, that is a warning sign about my heart, not proof I know enough.
try: Read one verse slowly today and stay with it until something in you responds.

title: They understood the words, then bent them anyway.
subtitle: Why knowing is not the same as accepting

picture.label: What some did with the Book

then: The believers in Madinah hoped the scholars around them would accept Islam. The verse lowers that hope. {trap}A party of them heard Allah's words, understood them, and changed their meaning while they knew.{/trap} Ibn Zayd said some would twist rulings for whoever paid.
now: You know what the verse says about honesty in trade. Then a deal comes and you find a reading that lets you off. Or you quote the part of a hadith that suits your argument in the family group chat. {trap}Bending is easier when you already understand.{/trap}
old: I know what it really means, I am just reading it flexibly.
new: Twisting a clear meaning to suit me is worse than not knowing it at all.
try: Think of one teaching you tend to stretch in your favour. Read it again as plainly as you can.

title: One face in public, another in private.
subtitle: Hiding the truth so you cannot be held to it
then: Some of them said we believe when they met the Muslims. {trap}In private they warned each other: do not share what Allah opened for you in your Book,{/trap} or it will be used against you before your Lord. Ibn Abbas said this was about the coming Prophet ﷺ foretold in their Book.
now: In the meeting you agree with the plan. In the corridor you tell a colleague it is nonsense. Or you know the facts that would settle a family dispute, but you keep them back because they hurt your side. {idea}Hiding the truth does not change it.{/idea}
old: What I say in private is my own business.
new: Truth I hide to win an argument still stands as witness against me.
try: Next time you notice your private words contradict your public ones, choose one and make them match.

title: Did they forget Allah was in both rooms?
subtitle: The private room is not private

row.title: there is no off the record

then: After quoting their private warning to each other, the verse asks one short question. {idea}Do they not know that Allah knows what they hide and what they show?{/idea} Al-Hasan said the hidden part was what they said when alone, away from the Companions.
now: You delete the message. You lower your voice. You close the office door before saying it. You plan so carefully what people will see. {idea}Allah is already in the room, before you shut the door.{/idea}
old: As long as no one hears, it does not count.
new: Allah hears the private version as clearly as the public one.
try: Before your next private conversation about someone, ask: would I say this if they could hear?

title: They did not know the Book, only their hopes about it.
subtitle: Religion built on guesses
then: After the scholars who twisted the Book, the verse names another group. {trap}They could not read it and knew only wishes and guesses.{/trap} Mujahid said they did not understand what came to Musa, yet spoke falsehood. Qatadah said they held wrong ideas about Allah.
now: Much of what you believe came from a forward on your phone, an uncle at a wedding, a clip with dramatic music. Some of it is true. Some is wishful. {idea}You have the Book itself, in your own language, a tap away.{/idea}
old: I know enough about my faith from what I have picked up.
new: What I picked up may be hope dressed as knowledge. I can check the source.
try: Take one belief you heard secondhand and look it up in the Quran or a trusted teacher today.

title: They wrote it themselves and sold it as Allah's word.
subtitle: Putting Allah's name on your own words
then: A third group did worse. {trap}They wrote their own words and said: this is from Allah,{/trap} to sell it for a small price. Al-Hasan said the small price is this world and all it holds. Ibn Abbas told Muslims not to ask such people, since {idea}they had the Quran, fresh and unchanged.{/idea}
now: You want people to do something, so you say Islam requires it, though you are not sure. You want to win a family argument, so you invent a hadith. {trap}Putting Allah's name on your own opinion is a heavy thing.{/trap} Say I think, when you only think.
old: It is fine to say Islam says so if it helps people behave.
new: Claiming Allah said what He did not say is one of the gravest lies.
try: Next time you are tempted to say Islam says, check if you are sure. If not, say I think instead.

title: We will only burn a few days. Says who?
subtitle: A comfortable claim with no promise behind it
then: Some claimed the Fire would touch them only for a few counted days. Ibn Abbas reported they said forty. The Prophet ﷺ was told to ask: {idea}did you take a covenant from Allah?{/idea} If so, He never breaks it. {trap}If not, you are saying about Allah what you do not know.{/trap}
now: I pray sometimes, I am from a good family, I will be fine. It is the voice that lets you skip the hard change today. {idea}Ask it the same question: who promised you that?{/idea} Real hope is built on what Allah actually said.
old: I will be fine in the end, whatever I do.
new: My hope should rest on what Allah promised, not on what I assume about myself.
try: Write down one easy assumption you make about your fate. Ask honestly where that promise came from.

title: Not wishes but deeds: sin can surround a person.
subtitle: How small wrongs pile up into a cage

row.title: it is only a small thing

then: The answer to their claim is: {idea}No, it is not as you wish.{/idea} Whoever earns evil and stays in it until sin surrounds him is among the people of the Fire. Ibn Kathir cites the Prophet ﷺ: {trap}beware of belittled sins, they gather on a person{/trap} like sticks gathered for a fire.
now: One white lie at work. One skipped prayer. One unkind joke in the group chat. Each one feels like nothing. {trap}Together they become the walls around you.{/trap} {reward}Repentance opens a gap in the wall every single time.{/reward}
old: It is only a small sin, it hardly counts.
new: Small sins gather like sticks. Repenting early keeps them from closing in.
try: Name one small habit you have stopped noticing as wrong. Ask Allah's forgiveness for it tonight.

title: Belief plus good deeds: that is the way into Paradise.
subtitle: The other side of the same scale
then: Right after the warning comes the promise. {reward}Those who believe and do good deeds are the people of Paradise, there forever.{/reward} Ibn Kathir links it to 4:123: {idea}it is not by your wishes, nor the wishes of the People of the Book.{/idea}
now: Not your surname. Not the mosque your father built. Not the badge on your profile. It is the quiet things: the prayer on a busy day, the honest invoice, the visit to a lonely neighbour. {reward}Those are what last.{/reward}
old: Being part of a good community will see me through.
new: Paradise is reached by belief that shows up in what I do.
try: Do one good deed today that nobody will ever know about.

title: Worship Allah, be good to people, speak kindly. Then most turned away.
subtitle: The covenant in one sentence
then: Allah reminds the Children of Israel of the covenant He took from them. {idea}Worship none but Allah. Be good to parents, relatives, orphans and the poor. Speak good to people.{/idea} Ibn Kathir notes Allah often pairs His right with the parents' right. {trap}Except a few, they turned away knowingly.{/trap}
now: You pray on time, then snap at your mother on the phone. You give charity online, then talk down to the cashier. The covenant holds these together. The Prophet ﷺ said: {reward}do not belittle any good, even meeting your brother with a cheerful face.{/reward}
old: As long as I do my prayers, how I talk to people is a separate matter.
new: Worship and kind speech are in the same covenant. One without the other is incomplete.
try: Call or message one parent or older relative today just to say something kind.

title: Do not shed each other's blood. They agreed, as witnesses.
subtitle: A promise made with eyes open
then: The covenant forbade them to kill one another or drive one another out of their homes. Ibn Kathir notes the words are literally your own selves, because {idea}people of one faith are like one soul.{/idea} He cites the Prophet ﷺ: believers are like one body. {trap}And they agreed to it as witnesses.{/trap}
now: The cousin you have not spoken to in years over an inheritance. The colleague from your own community you quietly push out of a job. {idea}Hurting your own is hurting yourself.{/idea} You signed up to this the day you said you believe.
old: This fight is with them, it has nothing to do with me.
new: When I harm my own people, I am wounding the body I belong to.
try: Think of one relative or fellow believer you are cold with. Send a simple greeting today.

title: They ransomed the captives they had helped capture.
subtitle: Believing in part of the Book
then: Before Islam, the Aws and Khazraj of Madinah fought often. Jewish tribes allied with each side, so {trap}they ended up killing and expelling their own.{/trap} After the war they ransomed their captives, as the Torah required. Ibn Abbas said this verse was about that. {idea}Do you believe in part and reject part?{/idea}
now: You fast every Ramadan and keep a contract you know is crooked. You are strict about halal meat and loose about your words in the group chat. {idea}It is easy to keep the rules that cost nothing.{/idea} The verse asks about the ones you skip.
old: I follow the parts of my religion that matter most to me.
new: Picking only the commands that suit me is believing in part and rejecting part.
try: Name one teaching you know but quietly ignore. Take one small step toward it today.

title: They bought this world and paid with the next.
subtitle: A bad trade, seen at its end
then: This sums up the previous verse. They broke the Book where it cost them and kept it where it was easy, all for worldly gain. Ibn Kathir: {trap}they preferred this life to the Hereafter.{/trap} So their punishment will not be lightened, nor will anyone help them.
now: You skip the prayer to close the deal. You cut a corner on the tax form. You stay quiet when you should speak because it might cost you the promotion. {idea}Each one is a small purchase.{/idea} Ask what you are paying with.
old: I will sort out the Hereafter later. Right now I need to get ahead.
new: Every time I trade the next life for this one, I am the one who loses.
try: Before one decision today, ask: what am I paying for this, and is it worth it?

title: Whenever a messenger said what they did not want, they grew arrogant.
subtitle: When truth collides with desire

row.title: it was not what they wanted

then: Allah gave Musa the Torah, then sent messengers after him, then Isa with clear signs, supported by the Holy Spirit, which Ibn Masud and others said is Jibril. Ibn Kathir: {trap}the messengers commanded what went against their desires,{/trap} so they denied some and killed others.
now: A friend tells you, gently, that you are wrong about something. A doctor says what you do not want to hear. Your child points out your temper. {trap}The urge is to attack the messenger.{/trap} {idea}The real question is whether it is true.{/idea}
old: I reject it because it is not convincing.
new: Often I reject it because it is inconvenient, not because it is false.
try: Recall the last hard truth someone told you. Consider it again without defending yourself.

title: Our hearts are wrapped, they said. It was not an excuse.
subtitle: Calling a closed heart a full one
then: They said their hearts were wrapped. Ibn Abbas and Mujahid said: covered, screened. Another reading from Ibn Abbas: {trap}our hearts are full of knowledge and need nothing from you.{/trap} The verse replies that {idea}it was their disbelief that sealed them,{/idea} so little did they believe.
now: I am just not a spiritual person. I already know all this. That is not for someone like me. {trap}They sound like humility or honesty, but they can be doors we close ourselves.{/trap} A closed heart usually started as a no.
old: Religion just does not reach me, that is how I am.
new: A heart closes from repeated refusals. It can open with small yeses.
try: Next time you think that is not for me, try one small piece of it anyway.

title: They prayed for him to come. When he came, they refused.
subtitle: Recognising the truth and still saying no
then: Before the Prophet ﷺ came, some of them told the Arabs of Madinah: {idea}a prophet is coming and with him we will defeat you.{/idea} Ibn Abbas said Muadh bin Jabal later reminded them of this. Abu Al-Aliyah said {trap}when they saw he was not one of them, they rejected him{/trap} though they knew.
now: You pray for a good husband for your daughter. One comes, kind and devout, but from a family or background you did not picture. You prayed for a job, and it came through someone you dislike. {idea}Sometimes the answer arrives in a form we did not order.{/idea}
old: I will accept the answer if it comes the way I expected.
new: When what I asked for arrives, I should not reject it for the wrapper it came in.
try: Think of one prayer that was answered in an unexpected form. Thank Allah for it today.

title: Envy that Allah gave His favour to someone else.
subtitle: Selling yourself for a grudge
then: As-Suddi said they sold themselves. The motive the verse names is {trap}resentment that Allah would send His favour on whom He wills.{/trap} Ibn Kathir: there is no envy worse than this. Abu Al-Aliyah explained the wrath upon wrath as their rejection of Isa, then of Muhammad ﷺ.
now: Your colleague gets the promotion. Your friend's child gets into the school yours did not. A sister gets married first. {trap}The question why her, not me can sour everything.{/trap} {idea}Allah's gifts to others take nothing from you.{/idea}
old: It is not fair that they got it instead of me.
new: Allah gives His favour to whom He wills. Resenting it only hurts me.
try: Think of someone whose blessing stings you. Make a sincere dua for them to have more of it.

title: Only what came to us, they said. Then why kill your prophets?
subtitle: A loyalty that does not hold up

row.title: we are loyal to our Book

then: Asked to believe in what Allah revealed, they said: {trap}we believe in what was sent to us.{/trap} But {idea}the new revelation confirmed what they had.{/idea} The Prophet ﷺ was told to ask: if you are true to your own Book, why did you kill the prophets who came upholding it?
now: We have always done it this way, says the uncle, about a custom the religion never asked for. Loyalty to tradition is good, until it becomes a shield against the truth. {idea}Ask whether you are loyal to the source, or only to what is familiar.{/idea}
old: I am loyal to what my people have always held.
new: Real loyalty to guidance means accepting truth when it comes, even from outside my circle.
try: Pick one family custom you defend. Check what the Quran or Sunnah actually says about it.

title: Musa brought clear proofs. They turned to a calf anyway.
subtitle: Forgetting so fast

row.title: clear proofs
sub: the sea, the staff, the hand

row.title: wrongdoers
sub: knowing there is no god but Allah

then: Ibn Kathir lists the signs: the flood, the locusts, the staff, the hand, the parted sea, the manna and quails. Yet when Musa went to the mountain, {trap}they took the calf as a god.{/trap} The verse calls them wrongdoers, because {idea}they knew there is no god but Allah.{/idea}
now: You came back from Umrah glowing. Three weeks later the phone is back in charge and the prayers are slipping. Or your teacher travels and the study circle falls apart. {trap}Some of us lean on the person, not on Allah.{/trap}
old: I am strong in faith when the right people are around me.
new: My faith should stand when the reminder-giver is away, not only when he is near.
try: Choose one practice you only do around others. Do it alone today.

title: We hear and we disobey. The calf had soaked into their hearts.
subtitle: When love of a thing drinks up the heart

row.title: what does it tell you to do?

then: Allah raised the mountain over them and said: {idea}hold firmly to what We gave you, and listen.{/idea} They said: we hear and we disobey. Qatadah said {trap}love of the calf soaked into their hearts{/trap} until it lived there. The verse asks: how bad is what your faith tells you to do?
now: You know the verse. You can recite it. And yet the thing you love more, the habit, the screen, the money, wins every time. {trap}Love that soaks in quietly can outvote what you know.{/trap} What a heart drinks, it starts to obey.
old: I know what is right, so I must be fine.
new: What my heart loves most decides what I do, more than what I know.
try: Notice one thing you reach for automatically today. Ask if it has soaked too deep.

title: If Paradise is only for you, why fear death?
subtitle: A claim tested against the heart

row.title: how you feel about meeting Him

then: Some claimed the home of the Hereafter was theirs alone. The Prophet ﷺ was told to answer: {idea}then wish for death, if you are truthful.{/idea} Ibn Abbas said it meant: call on Allah to bring death on whichever side is lying. {trap}They declined.{/trap}
now: It is easy to say I am fine with Allah in a discussion at the dinner table. The honest check is quieter. When you think of meeting Him tonight, do you feel ready, or do you want more time to fix things? {idea}That feeling tells you what to work on.{/idea}
old: I am sure I am on the right side, so I have nothing to worry about.
new: My real confidence shows in how I feel about meeting Allah, not in what I claim.
try: Ask yourself honestly: if I met Allah tonight, what would I want to have fixed? Start on it.

title: They will never wish it, because of what their hands sent ahead.
subtitle: Deeds go ahead of us
then: The verse answers its own challenge. {trap}They will never wish for death, because of what their hands have sent before them.{/trap} Ibn Kathir: because they knew the Prophet ﷺ was true, yet denied him. {idea}Allah knows the wrongdoers.{/idea}
now: Every message you send, every shift you work honestly or not, every kindness at home goes ahead of you like luggage on a flight. {idea}You will meet it at the other end.{/idea} The good news: you can still add to what goes ahead today.
old: What I did is in the past, it is behind me.
new: What I did has gone ahead of me, and I will meet it again.
try: Send one good deed ahead today on purpose: a charity, a visit, a sincere apology.

title: A thousand years would not move him one step from it.
subtitle: A long life is not an escape

row.title: only what I do with it

then: The verse describes {trap}people greedier for life than anyone, wishing to live a thousand years.{/trap} Ibn Abbas said long life would not save them from punishment. Ibn Zayd compared it to Iblis, whose long life did not help him. {idea}Allah sees what they do.{/idea}
now: The anti-ageing creams. The fear of birthdays. The plan to turn to Allah when you retire. {trap}Time alone fixes nothing.{/trap} {reward}A short life spent well is worth more than a long one spent running.{/reward}
old: If I just have more years, I will sort myself out.
new: More years only help if I change. Changing can start today.
